metadata.name: Proposed unified BEP scientific reference map
metadata.purpose: A source-linked semantic reconciliation of the preserved original and independent maps, updated with the later integrated research snapshot. It is a proposal and crosswalk; it does not rewrite or merge the input datasets.
metadata.scientific_compass: Under what physical, kinetic, mathematical, and experimental conditions can periodic inlet forcing improve cycle-averaged ethylene production or selectivity relative to an appropriately optimized feasible steady-state benchmark?

prior_source_map_crosswalk.use: Preserved prior semantic crosswalk; rows remain unchanged and are inherited by reference.

node_contract.id_policy: Preserve the shared root and discipline IDs. Proposed content themes use stable u_ IDs. Input map IDs and histories remain unchanged.
node_contract.evidence_policy: Separate source observation, source model/design result, mathematical derivation under assumptions, project hypothesis, and unverified source attachment.
node_contract.approval_policy: Structural placement and AI research maturity do not assert human understanding, human source verification, or map approval.

nodes.title: BEP scientific domain
nodes.summary: Dynamic acetylene semi-hydrogenation in a packed bed; periodic inlet forcing is evaluated against the best feasible steady operation under the same objective and constraints.
nodes.explanation: Scientific compass: under what catalyst, kinetic, transport, mathematical, control, and experimental conditions can inlet forcing improve cycle-averaged ethylene production or selectivity? This is a research question. No gain sign or magnitude is established.
assumptions: A proposed taxonomy preserves competing physical and mathematical models until target evidence discriminates them.
limitations: The target catalyst, feed, objective, actuator envelope, and validated predictive model remain unspecified.
open_questions: Which target-specific evidence will define a meaningful comparison?

nodes.title: Physics
nodes.summary: Reaction chemistry, catalyst state, kinetics, transport, thermal response, and physical measurement.
nodes.explanation: Physical causes are organized by the local catalyst and apparatus boundary. Source-specific mechanisms remain alternatives until target composition, support, pretreatment, and operating data are fixed.
limitations: The physical model and catalyst applicability remain open.
open_questions: Which physical states are needed at the first evidence-supported fidelity?

nodes.title: Mathematics
nodes.summary: Conservation, scales, numerics, periodic response, inference, uncertainty, and constrained optimization.
nodes.explanation: Mathematical statements retain their assumptions, units, domain, and status as derivation, approximation, or source-model result. Numerical correctness does not supply empirical validation.
limitations: Final balances, rate basis, solver, and uncertainty model depend on target choices.
open_questions: Which reductions and conditions are supported by target data?

nodes.title: Systems & Control
nodes.summary: Plant boundaries, input realization, excitation, measurement, observability, objectives, constraints, and evidence.
nodes.explanation: The system view connects manipulated commands to bed inputs and outlet observations. Experimental feasibility and performance comparison are separate from kinetic identification.
limitations: Hardware, measurement, safety, and success criteria are not specified.
open_questions: Which signals can be manipulated and measured at the required bandwidth?

nodes.title: Reaction network, pathways, and products
nodes.summary: The sequential C2H2 → C2H4 → C2H6 network defines an intermediate product and its main gas-phase over-hydrogenation loss; microscopic pathways and side products remain catalyst-specific.
nodes.explanation: Keep net stoichiometry separate from elementary surface chemistry and measured product accounting. Pd/PdAg surface calculations, Pd/Al2O3 rate fits, deposit-associated site models, and Pd–Mn substitution proposals give different route hypotheses. Include inlet ethylene, ethane, C4+ products, and retained carbon where the chosen system boundary and measurements require them.
equations: C2H2 + H2 → C2H4; C2H4 + H2 → C2H6 (net reactions, not elementary steps).
For species order (H2,C2H2,C2H4,C2H6), S = (−r1−r2,−r1,r1−r2,r2) under the two-reaction gas-only closure.
assumptions: Two net reactions form a minimum carbon-balance scaffold.
Non-detection means below method detection limits, not physical absence.
limitations: Source catalysts and reaction windows differ; C4+ and deposit inventories may be omitted in reduced models.
open_questions: Which carbon products and sinks are measurable over the target forcing range?
Which microscopic pathways are supported by the working catalyst?

nodes.title: Catalyst identity, active sites, and working-surface state
nodes.summary: Nominal Pd:Ag composition alone does not specify the active surface or site ensembles under reaction conditions.
nodes.explanation: Support, loading, particle size, pretreatment, carbonaceous deposits, hydrogen, and working-surface composition can change adsorption and pathway rates. A single-site Pd PSSA fit, a deposit-associated A/E model, a Pd–Mn substitution proposal, idealized Pd/PdAg surfaces, and a PdAg/TiO2 in-situ structure study answer different catalyst-specific questions.
equations: Site closure example: Σ_j θ_j = 1 for a stated site inventory and the species assigned to it.
assumptions: Site families and coverage variables must be defined for each kinetic model.
limitations: No source model uniquely identifies the BEP catalyst's working surface.
open_questions: What catalyst batch, support, geometry, preparation, pretreatment, and working-surface state define the target?

nodes.title: Kinetic law, thermal dependence, and surface-memory closures
nodes.summary: A transient reactor can use quasi-steady surface kinetics; explicit coverage dynamics are a separate closure requiring independent evidence and parameters.
nodes.explanation: Langmuir–Hinshelwood–Hougen–Watson rates and pseudo-steady-state surface balances algebraically eliminate coverages. Dynamic coverage ODEs retain adsorbate storage and require elementary rates, site conservation, and consistent gas/surface inventories. Arrhenius centering, parameter units, and source-level inconsistencies must be preserved. Slow campaign activity decay and fast within-cycle adsorbate memory occupy different state scales.
equations: k(T)=k(Tref) exp[−Ea/R(1/T−1/Tref)] when k(Tref) is the fitted reference rate.
θ̇ = r_adsorption − r_reaction − r_desorption only after each species/site balance is specified.
assumptions: Any kinetic closure is local to its catalyst, feed, temperature, pressure, and conversion domain.
limitations: Urmès 2019 reports conflicting K1 values in text and table; neither is resolved as target truth.
open_questions: Does the target transient require dynamic coverages, or can an evidence-supported PSSA closure predict outputs?
Which parameters are independently identifiable?

nodes.title: Packed-bed, pellet, and interphase transport
nodes.summary: Gas residence and dispersion, external films, intrapellet diffusion, and mixing filter the commanded composition before it reaches active sites.
nodes.explanation: A spatial bed model can include axial dispersion and variable superficial velocity; a pellet model can add radial diffusion and internal storage. Film and pellet omissions require target-specific screening and boundary conventions. Model-domain choices determine which mixer, line, inlet, and outlet dynamics appear as boundary conditions.
equations: J_i = u_s C_i − ε_b D_ax ∂z C_i.
ε_b ∂t C_i + ∂z J_i = S_i for a 1-D bed-volume balance with declared bases.
assumptions: C_i is void-gas concentration; u_s is superficial velocity; D_ax has units m²/s; source terms use a declared catalyst-mass basis.
limitations: The proposal's compact equation does not by itself define all boundary domains or target velocity closure.
open_questions: Are film, pellet, axial dispersion, and changing total flow material over the target operating envelope?
Which upstream/downstream volumes belong in the model?

nodes.title: Energy balance, thermal response, and catalyst evolution
nodes.summary: Exothermic heat release and campaign-time catalyst evolution may alter mean performance and cycle response at distinct timescales.
nodes.explanation: An isothermal model is an assumption requiring a temperature scale or measurement argument. Temperature forcing changes Arrhenius rates, while thermal inertia and heat removal filter the waveform. Catalyst deactivation during months of operation does not establish fast within-cycle adsorbate memory.
equations: A generic bed energy balance couples ρCp ∂tT, axial heat flux, reaction heat Σ_j(−ΔH_j)r_j, and wall heat exchange; each term needs a declared basis.
assumptions: Thermal properties and heat-transfer coefficients can be treated as known only after target evidence.
limitations: No target temperature field, heat-release bound, or deactivation law is calibrated.
open_questions: Is an isothermal approximation adequate at relevant conversion and forcing amplitude?
What campaign horizon and catalyst aging costs belong in the metric?

nodes.title: Measurements, instrumentation, and physical observables
nodes.summary: Analyzer, tubing, detector, and spectroscopy dynamics shape which physical signals are observed and with what delay or bandwidth.
nodes.explanation: Separate the material signal path from state estimation: MFCs, mixers, bed, outlet lines, chromatographs, and surface-sensitive probes each have transfer and sampling behavior. Modulation-excitation spectroscopy can detect selected surface species in appropriate systems. It does not establish observability of every internal state in the target bed.
equations: A measurement channel can be represented as y_m(t)=H_m(s)y_true(t)+noise only where a linear time-invariant approximation is justified.
assumptions: Sampling, calibration, and transfer functions are identified over the frequencies used.
limitations: Actual BEP actuator, analyzer, sampling, and noise models are absent.
open_questions: What are command-to-bed and bed-to-analyzer transfer functions?
Which physical observables resolve mechanism alternatives?

nodes.title: Stoichiometric and continuum conservation models
nodes.summary: A stoichiometric matrix, declared volume/mass basis, and conservative fluxes connect reaction rates to spatial gas inventories.
nodes.explanation: The two-reaction stoichiometric source is a useful reduced accounting basis. For a dispersive packed bed, component inventory and flux must use consistent bed/void and catalyst-mass conventions. If velocity varies, u_s C_i remains inside the spatial flux divergence; summing species equations tests total-flow closure.
equations: d n/dt = N r for a homogeneous inventory.
ε_b ∂t C_i + ∂z(u_s C_i − ε_b D_ax ∂zC_i) = (1−ε_b)ρ_p Σ_j ν_ij r_j for one stated bed/pellet-density convention.
assumptions: Cross-section averaging, porosity, density, and reaction-rate bases are explicitly defined.
limitations: Additional products, adsorbed storage, pressure drop, or temperature variation require additional balances and closures.
open_questions: Which total-flow, pressure, adsorption-storage, and side-product balances are needed for the target?

nodes.title: Dimensionless groups and timescale hierarchy
nodes.summary: Dimensionless transport and forcing ratios organize which physical processes can shape the response.
nodes.explanation: Useful comparisons include axial Péclet number, reaction-to-residence Damköhler number, pellet Thiele modulus, and ωτ for measured bed, actuator, sensor, thermal, and kinetic timescales. Their numerical values must be calculated with the target geometry and properties; a resonance-like window is a hypothesis rather than a universal rule.
equations: Pe_ax = u_s L/(ε_b D_ax) under the stated flux convention.
Da = τ_res/τ_rxn; ϖ_j = ω τ_j for a named dynamic timescale τ_j.
assumptions: Each dimensionless group is defined with a fixed geometry, basis, and characteristic time.
limitations: No target dimensions, transport coefficients, or kinetic relaxation times are established.
open_questions: Which timescale ratios overlap within feasible actuator and analyzer bandwidth?

nodes.title: Discretization, stiff integration, and numerical verification
nodes.summary: Conservative space discretization, time integration, and convergence checks are required before interpreting computed periodic performance.
nodes.explanation: A shared finite-volume face flux makes internal fluxes cancel when cell balances are summed. Stiff kinetics and transport may motivate implicit BDF/Radau methods. The integrated reference derives Co+2Fo≤1 as a scalar sufficient positivity condition for a uniform-grid explicit advection–diffusion update; it is not a general nonlinear-reaction stability guarantee.
equations: ε_b Δz dC_{i,k}/dt = J_{i,k−1/2}−J_{i,k+1/2}+Δz S_{i,k}.
For scalar constant-coefficient upwind advection and central diffusion: Co+2Fo≤1 is a sufficient nonnegative-weight condition.
assumptions: Uniform cells and fixed cell volumes for the stated flux-telescoping and scalar explicit bound.
limitations: No target simulator, grid/time-step convergence, stiffness analysis, or solver comparison is validated here.
open_questions: Which independent conservation, positivity, and refinement checks are required for the target model?

nodes.title: Periodic orbits, mean response, and conditional no-gain limits
nodes.summary: The sign of a periodic performance change depends on the model class, objective, mean-input condition, and constraints.
nodes.explanation: For a stable LTI system at settled periodic response, equal-mean input preserves the mean output. For a memoryless concave scalar response, Jensen's inequality gives mean f(u)≤f(mean u). If feasible periodic controls include all steady controls under identical constraints and objectives, optimization gives a weak no-worse bound. Nonlinear distributed reactors with state memory can yield positive, zero, or negative changes; none of the limits supplies a target gain estimate.
equations: Stable LTI: mean(y)=G(0) mean(u) at settled periodic response.
Static concave f: E[f(u)]≤f(E[u]).
Nested feasible sets: sup_{u∈U_periodic}J(u)≥sup_{u∈U_steady}J(u) only when U_steady embeds under identical constraints.
assumptions: The three limits have distinct assumptions and must not be combined into a universal conclusion.
limitations: No target kinetic/transport parameterization or optimized feasible-set comparison is available.
open_questions: Which nonlinear state and timescale couplings survive in the target plant?

nodes.title: Identifiability, sensitivity, and uncertainty
nodes.summary: Parameter identifiability, practical precision, model discrimination, and performance uncertainty are separate questions.
nodes.explanation: Sensitivity and Fisher information depend on the output model, input design, noise covariance, and prior parameter region. A model can fit measured trajectories while retaining parameter correlations or structural non-identifiability. Kinetic parameter precision is a design outcome and does not itself establish periodic process benefit.
equations: F(θ) ≈ Σ_k J_k(θ)^T R_k^{-1}J_k(θ), for a specified observation model and covariance R_k.
assumptions: Local covariance approximations require a specified likelihood/error model and informative operating region.
limitations: No target sensitivity, rank, parameter covariance, or uncertainty propagation has been calculated.
open_questions: Which target parameters and outputs are identifiable from feasible experiments?
How does model uncertainty affect gain sign?

nodes.title: Mathematical optimization and optimal-control formulations
nodes.summary: Steady and periodic controls require explicit objective functionals, feasible sets, periodic boundary conditions, and numerical optimality evidence.
nodes.explanation: Optimization theory belongs beside systems and control because waveform variables and physical constraints are jointly optimized, while the comparator remains a mathematical statement. Local algorithms may return stationary candidates whose value depends on initialization, parameterization, and constraints. Numerical Pareto fronts remain model-conditioned until globality or robust bounds are established.
equations: J_per(u,T)=T⁻¹∫₀ᵀ q(x(t),u(t))dt with x(0)=x(T).
J_SS*=sup_{u∈U_SS}J_SS(u); J_per*=sup_{u∈U_per}J_per(u), under matched objective, resource basis, and constraints.
assumptions: The periodic trajectory has reached a stable cycle and all actuator and plant constraints are included.
limitations: This explicit theme was added in the integrated map but currently has no child concepts there; optimal-control transcription, multipliers, Pareto continuation, and robustness need further development.
open_questions: What control parameterization and optimality evidence are appropriate for the target model?

nodes.title: Plant, input realization, and model boundary
nodes.summary: The manipulated command, bed-plane input, reactor, outlet line, and analyzer form one coupled physical input/output chain.
nodes.explanation: A source concentration waveform at a mass-flow controller is not automatically the waveform experienced by the catalyst. Mixing, total-flow coupling, pressure, residence-time distribution, piping, and measurement lines set plant boundaries and delay. Hardware feasibility determines the admissible control set.
equations: u_bed(t)=H_actuator,mixer,line(s) u_cmd(t) only for a justified transfer-function approximation.
assumptions: Every lumped transfer function corresponds to an identified physical subsystem and operating region.
limitations: The actual BEP hardware and transfer functions are unavailable in the source maps.
open_questions: Which controls can vary independently and within what rate/amplitude/safety limits?

nodes.title: Periodic excitation and kinetic discrimination
nodes.summary: Periodic perturbations can improve kinetic information in some systems; information gain and production gain remain distinct outcomes.
nodes.explanation: Frequency, amplitude, phase, and input channel should be selected against candidate model sensitivities and measured response bandwidth. Urmès et al. demonstrate periodic acetylene-flow experiments and fitted outlet prediction for a source-specific Pd/α-Al2O3 model. That precedent supports periodic kinetic study, with accessible source scope and no productivity-gain claim.
equations: A local sensitivity objective can maximize det(F(θ)) or minimize a declared prediction-variance functional subject to experiment constraints.
assumptions: The candidate model and uncertainty region are adequate for local design and the actuator realizes the intended perturbation.
limitations: The target system has no verified kinetic sensitivity design or measured forcing response.
open_questions: Which waveform components separate competing target models while respecting the plant bandwidth?

nodes.title: Cycle metric and optimized steady benchmark
nodes.summary: Yield, selectivity, and productivity rank periodic operation differently; a periodic result needs a matched optimized steady comparator.
nodes.explanation: Define product and feed bases before optimization. For a cycle, integrate molar flows and resource use over the settled period; a ratio of integrated amounts differs from the mean of instantaneous ratios. Include inlet ethylene in net production, impose conversion/selectivity floors when appropriate, and state campaign, energy, hydrogen, and aging costs.
equations: n_E,net = ∫₀ᵀ(F_E,out−F_E,in)dt.
S_E = n_E,net / n_A,reacted only when this denominator is defined and positive.
Compare J_per* with J_SS* under identical objective and feasible resource/safety limits.
assumptions: The plant reaches a repeatable periodic orbit; averaging and analyzer post-processing preserve molar balances.
limitations: The proposal objective and all matched constraints remain decisions; an arbitrary steady point is not the optimum.
open_questions: Which metric, feed basis, minimum conversion, and campaign horizon define success?

nodes.title: Observability, state estimation, and evidence classes
nodes.summary: Outlet signals constrain reactor states through model and sensor dynamics; selected catalyst species can be observed in specific laboratory systems.
nodes.explanation: Structural observability, practical reconstructibility under noise, and sensor availability are separate. Outlet-only data and finite bandwidth can make internal states difficult to distinguish, while modulation-excitation spectroscopy has detected selected surface species. Classify data as source observation, source-model result, derivation under assumptions, project hypothesis, or unverified attachment.
equations: For a linearized model, observability depends on (A,C); nonlinear state reconstruction depends on model, input, outputs, and operating trajectory.
assumptions: The sensor transfer model and noise/sampling assumptions are declared.
limitations: No whole-bed observability or target observer has been established.
open_questions: Which states are reconstructible from available target measurements?
Which independent data can discriminate alternative kinetic closures?

nodes.title: Feasibility, robustness, and evidence ladder
nodes.summary: Scientific gain requires physically feasible inputs, uncertainty-aware comparison, independent prediction, and eventually a matched experiment.
nodes.explanation: A hypothesis should advance through source scope, dimensional and conservation checks, model discrimination, parameter uncertainty, numerical convergence, robust steady/periodic optimization, held-out prediction, and matched experimental comparison. Process limits, safety, pressure, temperature, hydrogen supply, analyzer resolution, and catalyst campaign effects belong in the feasible set.
equations: A robust comparison may use inf_{θ∈Θ} [J_per*(θ)−J_SS*(θ)] under a declared uncertainty set Θ and identical constraints.
assumptions: Uncertainty sets and safety constraints are evidence-based and not chosen after inspecting the preferred waveform.
limitations: No simulator, optimizer, fit, or experiment was run in this map comparison.
open_questions: What evidence threshold and uncertainty criterion would support a target gain claim?

cross_links.relation: reaction stoichiometry and pathway hypotheses constrain rate-law choices
working-surface state changes candidate active sites and fitted kinetic closure
alternative site models create model-discrimination and identifiability questions
surface relaxation and thermal timescales constrain forcing-period ratios
mixer, line, bed, and analyzer domains determine the realized input and model boundary
bed and pellet transport terms define conservative inventory and flux conventions
finite-volume face fluxes must preserve the declared global balance
instrument transfer and sampling mediate state observability and estimation
input design changes information about model parameters
a waveform useful for parameter identification need not improve production
periodic response and no-gain bounds depend on the selected cycle metric and steady comparator
physical limits and uncertainty define the optimization feasible set

source_evidence.title: Microkinetic Modeling of Acetylene Hydrogenation Under Periodic Reactor Operation
source_evidence.supports: Small-amplitude periodic-flow experiments on Pd/α-Al2O3; parameter estimation and fitted outlet-composition histories for a source-specific single-site kinetic model.
source_evidence.limits: Accessible abstract/preview does not establish the full axial model scope, PdAg transfer, or productivity/selectivity gain.

source_evidence.title: Kinetic Study of the Selective Hydrogenation of Acetylene over Supported Palladium under Tail-End Conditions
source_evidence.supports: A steady single-site Pd/α-Al2O3 PSSA model for its tested tail-end conditions; text and parameter table preserve K1=611 Pa^-1 vs 13 Pa^-1 conflict.
source_evidence.limits: Does not establish target PdAg parameters or transient surface memory; K1 discrepancy remains unresolved in the source.

source_evidence.title: The Kinetic Model of Hydrogenation of Acetylene–Ethylene Mixtures over Palladium Surface Covered by Carbonaceous Deposits
source_evidence.supports: Model comparison and fitted A/E deposit-associated site-family kinetics for commercial Pd/α-Al2O3.
source_evidence.limits: Site geometry is a kinetic interpretation and model choice for a specific catalyst/conditions; it does not establish the same active sites for the BEP catalyst.

source_evidence.title: Kinetic regularities and mechanism of acetylene hydrogenation over PdMn catalyst
source_evidence.supports: Pd–Mn/Al2O3 TPD/QMS observations and a proposed adsorption-substitution model with an explicitly unknown fast step.
source_evidence.limits: The pathway, fitted constants, and conversion regime are catalyst- and protocol-specific; they do not establish a PdAg target mechanism.

source_evidence.title: An Experimental Approach on Industrial Pd-Ag Supported α-Al2O3 Catalyst Used in Acetylene Hydrogenation Process: Mechanism, Kinetic and Catalyst Decay
source_evidence.supports: Industrial-catalyst-specific kinetic tests, product network, and campaign-time activity/deactivation treatment.
source_evidence.limits: Campaign-time activity decay does not supply within-cycle adsorbate coverage dynamics; catalyst batch and operating conditions may differ from the BEP.

source_evidence.title: Hydrogenation of acetylene–ethylene mixtures over Pd and Pd–Ag alloys: First-principles-based kinetic Monte Carlo study
source_evidence.supports: Idealized Pd/PdAg surface pathway and kinetic alternatives.
source_evidence.limits: Model surface calculations do not identify the supported target catalyst’s working surface or transferable rate constants.

source_evidence.title: In Situ Surface Structures of PdAg Catalyst and Their Influence on Acetylene Semihydrogenation Revealed by High-Pressure X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy
source_evidence.supports: Condition-dependent surface structure evidence for a specific Pd1Ag3/TiO2 catalyst.
source_evidence.limits: Does not test periodic forcing or establish universal PdAg structure/performance.

source_evidence.title: Modelling forced periodic operation of catalytic reactors
source_evidence.supports: A model-specific counterexample: adsorption/desorption models in the paper predict no rate improvement under periodic operation.
source_evidence.limits: Does not imply zero gain for every kinetic model or reactor.

source_evidence.title: Cyclic operation of reaction systems: the influence of diffusion on catalyst selectivity
source_evidence.supports: A theoretical porous-pellet example where a frequency window improves selectivity under strong diffusion limitation.
source_evidence.limits: The result is example-specific and does not establish a target PdAg forcing window.

source_evidence.title: Comparison between two sufficient conditions for improvement of an optimal steady-state process by periodic operation
source_evidence.supports: Classical sufficient conditions for periodic improvement in an optimal process.
source_evidence.limits: Sufficient conditions are not necessary conditions and do not prove improvement for the BEP reactor.

source_evidence.title: Forced Periodic Reactor Operation Applied to Methanol Synthesis
source_evidence.supports: Cross-system methanol study separates same-time-average-feed reference experiments from model-based steady/periodic Pareto optimization; reports measured periodic advantage for a selected experiment.
source_evidence.limits: The chemistry, catalyst, and CSTR apparatus differ; neither its gain nor magnitude transfers to acetylene/PdAg.

source_evidence.title: Model-based design of transient flow experiments for the identification of kinetic parameters
source_evidence.supports: Fisher-information-based experiment design and parameter-precision analysis for transient-flow esterification data.
source_evidence.limits: Information-design result is model-conditioned and does not establish BEP identifiability or performance gain.

source_evidence.title: Sensitivity Enhancement and Dynamic Behavior Analysis by Modulation Excitation Spectroscopy: Principle and Application in Heterogeneous Catalysis
source_evidence.supports: Modulation-excitation spectroscopy and phase-sensitive detection for selected catalytic surface species.
source_evidence.limits: Does not prove full distributed packed-bed-state observability.

source_evidence.title: Numerical integration strategies of PFR dynamic models with axial dispersion and variable superficial velocity
source_evidence.supports: Variable-velocity and constant-velocity model forms and numerical comparison for a CaO-mayenite CO2 capture bed.
source_evidence.limits: Methodological example only; no quantitative transfer to acetylene hydrogenation.

source_evidence.title: On Danckwerts’ Boundary Conditions for the Plug-Flow with Dispersion/Reaction Model
source_evidence.supports: A competing boundary-condition interpretation in the accessible abstract.
source_evidence.limits: The full derivation is not inspected; no boundary equation is selected for the BEP apparatus.

source_evidence.title: Dynamic methods for catalytic kinetics
source_evidence.supports: Review of transient kinetic identification methods.
source_evidence.limits: Does not establish target-catalyst rates, surface timescales, or periodic gain.

source_evidence.title: Nanofluidization as affected by vibration and electrostatic fields
source_evidence.supports: Identifies the unrelated publication attached to the legacy DOI.
source_evidence.limits: Supports no catalytic-kinetics claim.

source_evidence.title: Continuous Flow Systems: Distribution of Residence Times
source_evidence.supports: Classical RTD framing for continuous-flow reactors.
source_evidence.limits: The abstract does not choose the BEP apparatus boundary condition.

source_evidence.title: Structural Identifiability of Dynamic Systems Biology Models
source_evidence.supports: General analytic ODE methods and distinction between structural identifiability and practical precision.
source_evidence.limits: No target reactor rank, observability, or parameter value follows.

source_evidence.title: BEP research proposal
source_evidence.supports: Project question and proposed model/experiment scope.
source_evidence.limits: A proposal is not evidence that its assumptions, simulation, or gain claim have been validated.

claim_reconciliations.synthesis: No universal sign follows from periodic forcing. Stable LTI, static concavity, and nested feasible-set results give distinct conditional limits. Nonlinear stateful operation may improve, match, or reduce a selected cycle metric.
do_not_infer: A target gain or universal null result.
That kinetic timescale matching alone is sufficient.

claim_reconciliations.synthesis: Urmès et al. 2022 report periodic acetylene-flow experiments on Pd/α-Al2O3 for model-based parameter estimation and outlet-composition prediction. Accessible abstract/preview does not establish a PdAg productivity gain or fully resolve axial model scope.
do_not_infer: The BEP target gain is established.

claim_reconciliations.synthesis: Single-site PSSA, deposit-associated A/E sites, Pd–Mn adsorption substitution, and PdAg LHHW or ideal-surface models describe different catalysts, conditions, and evidence classes. They remain alternatives pending target catalyst and transient data.
do_not_infer: One mechanism is universal or already target-validated.

claim_reconciliations.synthesis: The 2019 paper's text reports a calculated K1=611 Pa^-1 while Table 5 lists K1=13 Pa^-1 fixed. Preserve both until erratum, code, data, or author clarification resolves them.
do_not_infer: Either value is a BEP parameter.

claim_reconciliations.synthesis: DOI 10.1016/j.ces.2008.08.012 identifies nanofluidization; Berger et al.'s catalytic-kinetics review is DOI 10.1016/j.apcata.2008.03.020. The citation error does not determine whether attached equations are correct.
do_not_infer: DOI correction validates every inherited claim.

claim_reconciliations.synthesis: Dehghani et al.'s campaign-time catalyst-activity state does not constitute a within-cycle adsorbate-coverage state. Both may matter at different horizons.
do_not_infer: A slow deactivation law proves fast coverage memory.

claim_reconciliations.synthesis: Kaps et al. report a methanol periodic experiment against a selected same-time-average-feed steady reference and separately calculate model-based steady/periodic Pareto fronts. The empirical reference and modeled optimized comparator are different evidence classes.
do_not_infer: Methanol CSTR gain transfers to acetylene/PdAg.

claim_reconciliations.synthesis: Waldron et al.'s precision improvements are based on model-based Fisher-information design and parameter covariance analysis; measurements are observations, while estimated precision is a model/design result.
do_not_infer: Information gain establishes process-performance gain or target identifiability.

claim_reconciliations.synthesis: Danckwerts-type flux matching and Mott–Green's alternative interpretation depend on which external domains are included. The abstract-only alternative is retained as a question, not selected for the target apparatus.
do_not_infer: A boundary phrase uniquely fixes the target outlet condition.

claim_reconciliations.synthesis: Selected surface species can be detected in suitable modulation-excitation spectroscopy systems; outlet-only data do not prove full internal state observability or universal impossibility.
do_not_infer: Every internal state is directly measurable.

claim_reconciliations.synthesis: Periodic yield, selectivity, and productivity require explicit cycle-integrated definitions and comparison against an optimized feasible steady value under the same objective, resource basis, and constraints.
do_not_infer: Gain against an arbitrary nominal steady point.

unresolved_questions.question: Feed composition, pressure, temperature, conversion, and safety window.
Which K1 value was used in Urmès 2019 final calculations: 611 Pa^-1 in text or 13 Pa^-1 in Table 5?
Do target transients require dynamic surface states or does a PSSA closure predict the relevant output response?
Which site families, intermediates, and pathways are supported on the working catalyst?
Which C4+, retained carbon, and gaseous products must enter the measured carbon balance?
Which RTD, film, pellet, dispersion, and variable-flow effects matter over the forcing envelope?
Which mixer, line, bed, exit volume, and analyzer domains define boundary conditions?
Does reaction and forcing make superficial velocity vary materially?
What command-to-bed and bed-to-analyzer transfers, sampling, and noise apply?
Which cycle objective and campaign/resource basis defines success?
What constraints and inputs define the optimized steady comparator?
Does any gain survive target fitting, robust optimization, and held-out experimental validation?
Which conservation, positivity, mesh/time convergence, and solver checks apply to the chosen model?
Can inputs, internal states, and kinetic parameters be separately reconstructed from available signals?

decisions_requiring_owner_input.question: What exact Pd:Ag ratio, support, particle/egg-shell geometry, preparation, pretreatment, and working surface define the target?
decisions_requiring_owner_input.why: This selects which catalyst-specific pathway and kinetic evidence could apply.

decisions_requiring_owner_input.question: Should success be net ethylene productivity/yield, selectivity above a conversion floor, campaign performance, or a multiobjective front?
decisions_requiring_owner_input.why: Different denominators and resource accounting can reverse rankings.

decisions_requiring_owner_input.question: Which inlet variables can be independently actuated, and what amplitude, bandwidth, pressure, temperature, total-flow, hydrogen, and safety limits apply?
decisions_requiring_owner_input.why: These define the realizable waveform and fair feasible sets.

decisions_requiring_owner_input.question: Which PSSA/dynamic-coverage, dispersion, film/pellet, thermal, and boundary alternatives are supported by the available target evidence?
decisions_requiring_owner_input.why: The selected model determines the possible forcing mechanisms and predictions.

decisions_requiring_owner_input.question: What target-specific calibration, held-out dynamic prediction, uncertainty margin, and experimental match would support a gain claim?
decisions_requiring_owner_input.why: Map inclusion and numerical output do not constitute predictive or experimental validation.

source_access_summary.scope_note: Other records include project documents, repository files, metadata-only records, and legacy attachments. Counts are coverage descriptors, not evidence-weighted quality scores.

interpretation_boundaries.urmes2022: direct periodic acetylene estimation/prediction precedent; no target productivity gain established
interpretation_boundaries.campaign_deactivation: long-horizon catalyst state; distinct from within-cycle surface memory
interpretation_boundaries.mathematical_no_gain: each result applies only under its stated model assumptions
interpretation_boundaries.model_comparison: the kinetic families are source-conditioned alternatives; none is promoted as target truth
interpretation_boundaries.historical_attachments: prior attachments are provenance leads; a citation edge does not prove claim support
